games.title: Cuphead
games.note: Hand-drawn in the style of 1930s cartoons by brothers Chad and Jared Moldenhauer, with a jazz score played by live musicians.

games.title: Alien Soldier
games.note: A run-and-gun made almost entirely of boss fights. It held the record for most bosses in a run-and-gun: 25.

games.title: Super Meat Boy
games.note: A hard, fast platformer by two developers, featured in Indie Game: The Movie.

games.title: Stubbs the Zombie in Rebel Without a Pulse
games.note: You play the zombie, eating brains to build a horde in a retro-futurist 1959 town. Built on the Halo engine.

games.title: Twin Cobra
games.note: A vertical helicopter shooter, called Kyukyoku Tiger in Japan. Its studio, Toaplan, later made Batsugun.

games.title: Payday 3
games.note: Moved the crew to New York. Its always-online launch in September 2023 was hit by server problems.

games.title: Tom Clancy's The Division 2
games.note: Moved the outbreak story to a summer Washington, D.C., months after the first game.

links.took: Its name and first concept: Quake was a hammer-wielding character in Carmack's D&D campaign.
links.added: Became a dark, fully 3D shooter with Lovecraftian monsters and online play.
links.extra: Wikipedia says the game was originally inspired by a D&D campaign among id Software staff.

links.took: Puzzles you solve without losing speed, and a mystery-driven story, both inspired by Half-Life.
links.added: A buddy story between a pilot and his Titan, BT, with wall-running platforming.
links.extra: The team wanted the campaign to feel unlike other shooters, especially Call of Duty.

links.took: Puzzles that keep a certain level of speed, which the team credited to BioShock and Half-Life.
links.added: Wall-running platforming set pieces between firefights, built to keep momentum.

links.took: Puzzle-like level design; the developers say Portal also influenced the game.
links.added: A time-shifting level where you jump between past and present mid-fight.
links.extra: A critic compared that level, Effect and Cause, favorably with Portal.

links.took: The push to try again: the Moldenhauers restarted their project after Super Meat Boy's indie success.
links.added: Hand-drawn 1930s cartoon animation and a run-and-gun built around boss fights.
links.extra: The brothers had first tried a game in this style around 2000.

links.took: A run-and-gun made of boss fights; Cuphead set out to beat Alien Soldier's record of 25.
links.added: Planned more than 30 bosses, plus airplane shooting stages, in Fleischer-style cartoon art.

links.took: The Halo engine, licensed to Wideload, the studio of Bungie co-founder Alexander Seropian.
links.added: You play the zombie: eat brains, possess people and grow a horde.

links.took: Toaplan's helicopter shooting; Seibu borrowed from Twin Cobra along with Xevious and 1942.
links.added: Swapped helicopters for fighter jets, with a spread Vulcan shot and a piercing laser.

links.took: Fast, momentum-based movement, which Wikipedia says Ultrakill draws on with Doom Eternal.
links.added: Slides, wall jumps and ground slams, plus coin-flip trick shots with a revolver.

links.took: Half-Life was one of the older shooters Szymanski grew up on and named a major inspiration.
links.added: A fast retro shooter with occult backwoods horror, published by New Blood.

links.took: The four-person heist crew, masks and stealth-or-loud jobs.
links.added: A New York setting, new heists and online-only matchmaking.

links.took: Massive's cover-based looter shooter and its Dark Zone.
links.added: Washington, D.C. in summer, eight-player raids and a deeper endgame.
